description: Instagram Reels published through the Content Publishing API. This is the only Instagram surface with precise, file-measurable hard requirements; a spec violation is rejected by the API at container creation.
byte_convention: Decimal bytes (1 MB = 1,000,000). Meta does not state binary or decimal; the decimal reading is the conservative one for a ceiling, so PreflightQC never passes a file Instagram would reject.
caveats: These rules are scoped to the API-publishing path. Organic in-app posting and paid placements tolerate more.
The Reels-tab eligibility window (5-90 s, 9:16) is a discovery condition, not an acceptance requirement, and is reported as a warning only.
Meta publishes no audio loudness target and no HDR/colour-space input requirement. Both are reported as unknown rather than guessed.
Closed GOP and edit-list absence are documented API requirements, but verifying them needs packet- and atom-level inspection beyond what PreflightQC V1 measures.

sources.title: IG User Media reference (Reel Specifications), Meta for Developers
Engineering at Meta, Bringing HDR video to Reels

rules.explanation: The Content Publishing API accepts MOV or MP4 (MPEG-4 Part 14) containers only.
The video track must be encoded with HEVC or H.264.
The video must be progressive. Interlaced content is not accepted.
rules.note: Scan type is read from container flags rather than from the picture, so it is reported as unknown unless an inspector positively identifies interlacing.

rules.explanation: Chroma subsampling must be 4:2:0.
Frame rate must be between 23 and 60 FPS.
Maximum 1920 horizontal pixels.
Aspect ratio must be between 0.01:1 and 10:1.
rules.note: The Reels lower bound is 0.01:1. Instagram Stories states 0.1:1 in the same document; PreflightQC preserves both values verbatim rather than normalising them.

rules.explanation: A 9:16 aspect ratio is recommended for Reels.
rules.message_fail: This is a recommendation, not an upload requirement. A Reel with a different aspect ratio can still be published.

rules.explanation: Video bitrate must not exceed 25 Mbps (VBR).
Duration must be at least 3 seconds and at most 15 minutes.
rules.note: The in-app Reels editor caps creation at 3 minutes, which is a different surface from the publishing API.

rules.explanation: Maximum file size is 300 MB.
rules.note: Some third-party integrator documentation cites 100 MB. That figure is not authoritative; the published API limit is 300 MB.

rules.explanation: Where an audio track is present it must be AAC.
Audio sample rate must not exceed 48 kHz.
Audio must be mono or stereo (1 or 2 channels).
An audio bitrate of 128 kbps is recommended.
rules.message_fail: This is a recommendation. A lower audio bitrate does not prevent publishing.

rules.explanation: The moov atom must be at the front of the file (fast start).
The container must contain no edit lists.
rules.note: Detecting edit lists needs atom-level inspection, which PreflightQC V1 does not perform; this is therefore reported as unknown rather than judged.

rules.explanation: The API documents a closed-GOP requirement.
rules.note: Verifying GOP structure needs packet-level analysis, which is beyond what PreflightQC V1 measures.

rules.explanation: Only Reels between 5 and 90 seconds are eligible to appear in the Reels tab.
rules.message_fail: This affects discovery in the Reels tab only. It is not an upload requirement and does not prevent publishing.

rules.explanation: Only Reels with a 9:16 aspect ratio are eligible to appear in the Reels tab.
rules.message_fail: This affects discovery in the Reels tab only. It is not an upload requirement and does not prevent publishing.

rules.explanation: Colour transfer characteristics, reported for information.
rules.note: Meta accepts HDR uploads and tone-maps them server-side, but publishes no creator-facing HDR or colour-space input requirement. PreflightQC therefore reports the value without judging it.

rules.explanation: The in-app Reels editor supports creating videos up to 3 minutes.
rules.note: This is a different surface from the publishing API, whose limit is 15 minutes. Both figures are reported; neither is silently preferred.
